text: An agreement enforceable by law is a
subject: Business Law
explanation: A contract is an agreement that creates legal obligations.

text: The minimum age at which a person can enter into a valid contract in India is
subject: Business Law
explanation: Under the Indian Majority Act a person attains majority at eighteen.

text: A proposal when accepted becomes a
subject: Business Law
explanation: Acceptance of an offer converts the proposal into a promise.

text: An agreement without consideration is always void
subject: Business Law
explanation: There are exceptions such as gifts and natural love and affection where consideration is not required.

text: List the essential elements of a valid contract
subject: Business Law
correctAnswer: Offer and acceptance lawful consideration capacity free consent lawful object and certainty.
explanation: These elements must all be present for a valid contract.

text: Explain the modes of discharge of a contract
subject: Business Law
correctAnswer: A contract is discharged by performance mutual agreement impossibility lapse of time operation of law and breach. Each brings the obligations to an end.
explanation: Cover the various ways contractual obligations terminate.

text: A contract to compensate a party for loss caused by another is a contract of
subject: Business Law
explanation: Indemnity promises to make good a loss suffered by another.

text: The person whose goods are delivered to another for a purpose on return is the
subject: Business Law
explanation: In bailment the bailor delivers goods to the bailee for a purpose on return.

text: A contract of guarantee involves three parties
subject: Business Law
explanation: Guarantee involves the creditor principal debtor and surety.

text: Distinguish between indemnity and guarantee
subject: Business Law
correctAnswer: Indemnity involves two parties and one promise while guarantee involves three parties and a secondary liability of the surety.
explanation: Guarantee has an extra party and a contingent liability.

text: Explain the rights and duties of a bailee
subject: Business Law
correctAnswer: A bailee must take reasonable care of the goods and return them as agreed and has the right to recover expenses and claim a lien for unpaid charges.
explanation: Cover the duties of care and return and the rights of reimbursement.

text: The Act that governs contracts for the sale of movable goods is the
subject: Business Law
options: Sale of Goods Act|Companies Act|Partnership Act|Contract Act
explanation: The Sale of Goods Act 1930 governs contracts for the sale of goods.

text: The transfer of ownership of goods for a price is called a
subject: Business Law
explanation: A sale transfers property in goods from seller to buyer for a price.

text: In a contract of sale property in the goods passes immediately to the buyer
subject: Business Law
explanation: In a sale ownership passes at once while in an agreement to sell it passes later.

text: Distinguish between a sale and an agreement to sell
subject: Business Law
correctAnswer: In a sale property in goods transfers immediately while in an agreement to sell it transfers at a future time or on a condition.
explanation: The timing of ownership transfer is the key difference.

text: Explain the doctrine of caveat emptor and its exceptions
subject: Business Law
correctAnswer: Caveat emptor means let the buyer beware so the buyer must examine goods before purchase. Exceptions arise for fitness for purpose merchantable quality and sale by sample.
explanation: State the rule then the exceptions protecting the buyer.

text: A written promise to pay a fixed sum of money on demand is a
subject: Business Law
explanation: A promissory note is an unconditional written promise to pay a fixed sum.

text: A bill of exchange contains an order to pay whereas a promissory note contains a
subject: Business Law
explanation: A bill orders payment while a note promises payment.

text: A cheque is a bill of exchange drawn on a banker and payable on demand
subject: Business Law
explanation: A cheque is a special bill of exchange drawn on a banker payable on demand.

text: Define a negotiable instrument and list its types
subject: Business Law
correctAnswer: A negotiable instrument is freely transferable by delivery and includes promissory notes bills of exchange and cheques.
explanation: These instruments can pass from person to person freely.

text: Explain the distinction between a bill of exchange and a cheque
subject: Business Law
correctAnswer: A cheque is always drawn on a banker and payable on demand while a bill may be drawn on any person and may be payable after time. A cheque needs no acceptance but a bill usually requires it.
explanation: Cover the drawee payable on demand and acceptance differences.

text: A company is an artificial legal person created by
subject: Business Law
explanation: A company is a legal person created by law distinct from its members.

text: The document that defines the external objects and powers of a company is the
subject: Business Law
explanation: The memorandum states the objects and scope of the company.

text: A company has perpetual succession meaning its existence continues regardless of member changes
subject: Business Law
explanation: Perpetual succession means the company continues despite changes in membership.

text: State the characteristics of a company
subject: Business Law
correctAnswer: Separate legal entity perpetual succession limited liability common seal and transferable shares.
explanation: These features distinguish a company from other forms of business.

text: Explain the doctrine of separate legal entity with reference to a leading case
subject: Business Law
correctAnswer: A company is distinct from its members as held in Salomon versus Salomon. Shareholders are not personally liable for company debts beyond their shares.
explanation: Explain the corporate veil and the Salomon principle.

text: The Act that protects consumers against unfair trade practices is the
subject: Business Law
options: Consumer Protection Act|Contract Act|Sale of Goods Act|Companies Act
explanation: The Consumer Protection Act safeguards consumer rights and provides redressal.

text: The three tier consumer dispute redressal machinery ends at the
subject: Business Law
explanation: District State and National Commissions form the three tiers.

text: The Competition Act aims to prevent anti competitive agreements and abuse of dominance
subject: Business Law
explanation: The Competition Act 2002 regulates anti competitive practices and combinations.

text: List any four consumer rights
subject: Business Law
correctAnswer: Right to safety information choice to be heard and redressal.
explanation: These rights protect consumers in the marketplace.

text: Explain the objectives of the Consumer Protection Act
subject: Business Law
correctAnswer: The Act protects consumers from unfair trade practices and defective goods and services and provides simple speedy and inexpensive redressal of grievances.
explanation: Cover protection and the redressal machinery.

text: Assertion: A minor cannot enter into a valid contract. Reason: The law presumes a minor lacks the capacity to contract
subject: Business Law
options: Both assertion and reason are true and reason explains assertion|Both are true but reason does not explain assertion|Assertion is true but reason is false|Assertion is false but reason is true
explanation: Incapacity of minors makes their agreements void ab initio.

text: Match the instrument to its nature
subject: Business Law
options: Cheque - drawn on a banker|Promissory note - an order to pay|Bill of exchange - a promise to pay|Receipt - a negotiable instrument
explanation: A cheque is drawn on a banker while a note is a promise and a bill is an order.

text: Consent obtained by threatening harm is obtained by
subject: Business Law
explanation: Coercion involves threats to obtain consent unlawfully.

text: The person who is represented by an agent is called the
subject: Business Law
explanation: The principal authorises the agent to act on his behalf.

text: The Sale of Goods Act applies to immovable property
subject: Business Law
explanation: The Act applies only to movable goods and not to immovable property.

text: Explain the conditions and warranties in a contract of sale
subject: Business Law
correctAnswer: A condition is essential to the contract and its breach allows repudiation while a warranty is collateral and its breach only allows damages.
explanation: The remedy differs because conditions are more fundamental.

text: Explain the types of companies under the Companies Act
subject: Business Law
correctAnswer: Companies may be classified by incorporation as chartered statutory or registered by liability as limited or unlimited and as private or public.
explanation: Classify companies on the bases of incorporation liability and membership.

text: Read the case: A offers to sell his car to B for 200000 but B replies accepting at 180000. Explain the legal position of Bs reply
subject: Business Law
correctAnswer: Bs reply is a counter offer which rejects the original offer. No contract is formed and B cannot later accept the original offer unless A renews it.
explanation: A counter offer destroys the original offer.

text: Read the case: A company sells a defective machine that injures a worker despite a disclaimer in the contract. Explain whether the consumer can claim under consumer law
subject: Business Law
correctAnswer: The consumer can claim for a defective product and unfair practice as the right to safety and redressal cannot be excluded by a disclaimer under the Consumer Protection Act.
explanation: Statutory consumer rights override contractual disclaimers.

text: The concept of a company having a personality distinct from its members is called
subject: Business Law
explanation: The corporate veil separates the company from its shareholders.

text: Explain the concept of free consent and the factors vitiating it
subject: Business Law
correctAnswer: Free consent means agreeing without coercion undue influence fraud misrepresentation or mistake. Any of these factors makes consent not free and may make the contract voidable.
explanation: Cover each vitiating factor and its effect on the contract.

text: A contract entered into by an agent within authority binds the principal
subject: Business Law
explanation: An agent acting within authority binds the principal to third parties.

text: Explain the rights of an unpaid seller
subject: Business Law
correctAnswer: An unpaid seller has rights against the goods including lien stoppage in transit and resale and rights against the buyer for the price and damages.
explanation: Distinguish rights against goods from rights against the buyer.

text: Define consideration and state its legal rules
subject: Business Law
correctAnswer: Consideration is something of value given in return for a promise and must be real lawful and need not be adequate.
explanation: Consideration must move at the desire of the promisor and be lawful.

text: Explain the procedure for the incorporation of a company
subject: Business Law
correctAnswer: Incorporation requires filing the memorandum and articles with the registrar paying fees and obtaining the certificate of incorporation which gives the company legal existence.
explanation: Trace the steps from documents to the certificate of incorporation.

text: The winding up of a company brings its existence to an end
subject: Business Law
explanation: Winding up liquidates assets and ends the companys existence.

text: Explain the meaning and kinds of agency
subject: Business Law
correctAnswer: Agency is the relationship where an agent acts for a principal. It may arise by express or implied agreement ratification or necessity.
explanation: Describe the modes by which agency is created.

text: A bill of exchange that is payable at sight is called a demand bill
subject: Business Law
explanation: A demand bill is payable immediately on presentation.

text: Explain the remedies available to a consumer under the Consumer Protection Act
subject: Business Law
correctAnswer: Consumers may seek removal of defects replacement refund of price compensation and cessation of unfair practices through the district state or national commissions.
explanation: Cover the remedies and the redressal forums.
